title: Dynamic Embedding Capacity Manager and Fair Admission Controller
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a demand-aware capacity manager and fair admission controller for the embeddings endpoint to: improve p95/p99 latency under bursty multi-tenant traffic, reduce overall GPU cost by smarter warm-pool and shard scaling, and avoid noisy-neighbor degradation by enforcing per-tenant fairness and backpressure.

Background:
Recent incidents (see dashboards linked below) show embedding tail latency spikes when several mid-to-large tenants burst concurrent batch requests. Current autoscaler reacts slowly (scale-up delta of 90s) and the single global queue causes unfair head-of-line blocking. We also observed cost inefficiencies with cold-shot scale-ups and repeated short-lived workers.

Goals:
- Reduce p99 tail latency by 20-40% for top 10 tenants during burst windows.
- Keep steady-state cost within 10% of today while improving tail behavior.
- Provide predictable per-tenant SLOs via admission control and soft-fallbacks.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting serving runtime kernels (out of scope).
- Large re-architecture of embedding model sharding strategy (we will integrate with existing shard APIs).

Proposed design (high level):
1) Demand Estimator (short horizon): lightweight forecasting using exponentially-weighted recent qps and recurrence for burst detection (90s horizon). Outputs per-tenant demand score and request burstiness signal.
2) Predictive Scaler / Warm Pool Manager: uses demand estimator to pre-warm up to N hot workers (GPU shards) with aggressive early-stage criteria but conservative deprovisioning to avoid churn. Warm pool size is tenant-aware: critical tenants can reserve warm slots via config.
3) Fair Admission Controller (FAC): multi-queue admission with three bands (high-priority reserved, proportional fair, opportunistic). Admission decisions are based on token buckets per-tenant derived from recent spend + SLA tier. FAC enforces a short circuit for tiny low-latency requests (<200 tokens) to reduce tail for latency-sensitive workloads.
4) Queueing improvements: replace single FIFO global queue with tenant-aware multi-queue and a small global overflow queue. Introduce queue smoothing to avoid synchronized bursts.
5) Backpressure & Load-shedding: graceful rejection paths for over-capacity with structured error codes and suggested retry-backoff headers. On severe overload, opportunistic requests can be downgraded to smaller batch sizes or rerouted to a lower-cost model variant.
6) Metrics & Signals: new signals (per-tenant queue-time, admission-drop-rate, warm-pool-hit-rate, predicted-demand vs actual) will feed autoscaler and SLO dashboards.

API and Config surface:
- Console flags and API: tenant_reservation{boolean}, reservation_size{int}, priority_tier{standard|premium|critical}, admission_mode{strict|lenient|adaptive}.
- New metrics exported in Prometheus: embedding_fac_queue_time_seconds, embedding_fac_rejects_total, embedding_warm_pool_size, embedding_predicted_demand_total.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary (10% traffic) shows p99 improvement >= 15% for at least two burst scenarios in staging.
- No more than 5% increase in steady-state 24h cost during canary.
- Clear rollback plan and automated circuit breaker if error-rate or p99 regresses.

Testing / Validation plan:
- Synthetic multi-tenant burst tests using the existing benchmark harness (scenarios: 50 small tenants burst, 5 large tenants burst, mixed steady + burst).
- Chaos test: kill 1/3 of active shards during a controlled burst to validate admission and warm-pool behavior.
- Load test with mixed batch sized requests to validate tiny-request fast-path.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: internal traffic only (engineers + select customers) for 2 weeks.
- Beta: 10% production traffic with telemetry gating.
- GA: gradual ramp to 100% with automatic scaling enabled and weekly post-rollout metric review.

Observability / Dashboards:
- New dashboard: "Embedding FAC - Admission & Warmpool" (links below). Alerts: sustained queue_time > 300ms, warm_pool_hit_rate < 60% for > 10m, admission_reject_rate > 1% for > 5m.

Risks and mitigations:
- Forecasting misses could cause unnecessary warm pool spend: mitigate with conservative warm thresholds and post-hoc auto-eviction.
- Complexity in multi-queue fairness policy causing regressions: start with simple proportional share based on recent tokens and iterate.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should warm-pool pre-warms be vs. cost sensitivity? (propose default conservative + tenant opt-in for reservations)
- Should we expose per-tenant QoS tokens on the billing dashboard? (ops + billing alignment required)

Links and artifacts:
- Dashboard (staging): https://grafana.redwood.company/d/embeddings/fac-staging
- Benchmark harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/pull/412
- Design note (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.company/display/ENG/Embedding+FAC+Design
- Example rollout runbook (Drive): https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/embedding-fac-runbooks

Next steps:
- (This ticket) Implement FAC core and warm-pool manager in the autoscaler service.
- Add metrics instrumentation and initial console flags.
- Create canary job and benchmark scenarios for alpha testing.
